specification.problem: Discrete-time coined quantum walk on a finite one-dimensional chain whose edges are randomly present or absent in each time step (dynamic percolation). The evolution of the averaged density operator is a random unitary map, and the goal is the long-time (asymptotic) behaviour of the walker, obtained via the attractor structure of the random unitary map.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Scoped to the smallest useful construction: a coined quantum walk on a path graph of N vertices with Hadamard coin, edges independently open with probability p in each step, reflecting (coin-flipping) shift on broken edges and at chain ends. Tiny explicit instance: N=4 (2 position qubits, 1 coin qubit), p=1/2, walker started at x=1 with coin |R>. Deliverables: the one-step unitaries U_K, the random unitary map Phi, the attractor equations, and the asymptotic-state formula, plus a sampling protocol to estimate Phi^t. Out of scope: the paper's literature review, the explicit attractor basis for the 1D chain (not derivable from the abstract alone), the paper's concrete step-by-step numerical example, and all two-dimensional integer-lattice / Grover-coin results.

equations.label: Hilbert space, basis ordering and percolation distribution
equations.description: Position register (binary encoding of x, most significant) tensored with a coin qubit (L=0, R=1). Each edge is independently present with probability p in every step, giving the product distribution pi(K) over configurations.
equations.abstract_quote: the connections appear and disappear randomly in each step during the time evolution
equations.justification: The abstract specifies random, per-step appearance/disappearance of connections; independent Bernoulli edges with parameter p is the standard dynamic-percolation model implied. Coined position-coin Hilbert space is the standard quantum-walk setting.
assumptions: Edges are independent and identically distributed with probability p each step
Coined (discrete-time) quantum walk with a two-dimensional coin

equations.label: Configuration-dependent shift with reflection on broken edges
equations.description: If the edge in the direction of motion is present the walker moves; if the edge is absent (or the walker is at a chain end) it stays and its coin is flipped (reflection). S_K is a permutation of the basis, hence unitary.
equations.justification: The abstract does not state how the walker behaves at a missing edge; the reflecting (coin-flip) rule is a common choice in percolation quantum-walk literature and keeps S_K unitary. Other rules (e.g. phase-free staying without coin flip) would change the attractor structure.
assumptions: Reflecting boundary rule at broken edges and at chain ends
Finite chain with no periodic wrap-around

equations.label: One-step unitary and random unitary map
equations.description: Coin then shift for a fixed configuration; averaging over the per-step configuration gives a random unitary (unital) channel, iterated t times for the averaged state.
equations.abstract_quote: applying the asymptotic methods concerning random unitary maps
equations.justification: The abstract identifies the averaged dynamics as a random unitary map; with per-step i.i.d. configurations the averaged state is exactly the t-fold iterate of the single-step convex mixture of unitaries.
assumptions: Configurations are resampled independently each step (Markovian, memoryless)

equations.label: Attractor equations
equations.latex: U_K\,X\,U_K^{\dagger}=\lambda\,X\quad \forall K\text{ with }\pi(K)>0,\qquad |\lambda|=1\ \Longleftrightarrow\ U_K X=\lambda X U_K
equations.description: Operators X in the peripheral spectrum of Phi (eigenvalue of unit modulus) are exactly those satisfying the simultaneous intertwining relations for all unitaries in the mixture; these span the asymptotic (attractor) space.
equations.justification: Known result for random unitary maps (Novotny-Alber-Jex type attractor theory): unital channel, peripheral eigenvectors are common eigenoperators of all Kraus unitaries. Recalled as background, not extracted from the paper.
assumptions: 0<p<1 so that all configurations have positive probability; if p=1 only K=E contributes

equations.label: Asymptotic (long-time) averaged state
equations.description: After the contributions of eigenvalues with |lambda|<1 have decayed, the averaged state is the projection of rho_0 onto the attractor space, with possibly non-stationary (oscillating) terms from lambda not equal to 1. The limit is an asymptotic approximation for finite t, exact only as t tends to infinity.
equations.justification: Standard asymptotic formula for random unitary maps given a Hilbert-Schmidt-orthonormal attractor basis; this is the 'asymptotic method' the abstract refers to but the explicit attractors for the 1D chain are a paper result not available here.
assumptions: Attractors can be chosen Hilbert-Schmidt orthonormal (Phi is unital so the peripheral part is diagonalizable)

equations.label: Tiny explicit instance
equations.description: Three-qubit instance: 2 position qubits encoding x in {0,1,2,3}, 1 coin qubit; 8 equiprobable edge configurations; walker starts at vertex 1 pointing right.
equations.justification: No experiment scope was supplied; this is the smallest qubit-encodable chain with internal edges, chosen to make all 2^{N-1}=8 configurations explicit. The abstract says 'one dimensional chains' but does not give N, p, the coin, or initial state.

registers.name: pos
registers.role: binary encoding of the walker position x in {0,1,2,3}; placed first (most significant) in |x,c>

steps.description: Prepare the position and coin registers in the localized initial state of eq_6.
For each time step s=1..t: classically sample a configuration K_s from pi(K) (each edge kept with probability p).
Apply the coin operator C to the coin qubit.
Apply the configuration-dependent conditional shift S_{K_s} (move along present edges, coin-flip reflection at absent edges and chain ends), completing U_{K_s}.
Repeat coin+shift for t steps; averaging the resulting states over many independent configuration sequences realizes rho(t)=Phi^t(rho_0).
Classically (not on the circuit): solve the attractor equations for the 8 unitaries U_K and project rho_0 to obtain the predicted asymptotic state for comparison with large-t sampled statistics.

specification.measurement: Measure the position register (and optionally the coin qubit) in the computational basis at the final step; repeat over many shots and many independently sampled configuration sequences to estimate P_t(x)=<x|Tr_coin rho(t)|x>.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Average measured position histograms over configuration samples to estimate the diagonal of Phi^t(rho_0); compare with the long-time prediction from eq_5 obtained by classically solving eq_4 for the attractor space of the 2N x 2N unitaries U_K. Note that eq_5 is an asymptotic statement; finite-t estimates differ by decaying transient terms.
assumptions: Dynamic percolation modelled as i.i.d. Bernoulli(p) edges resampled every step
Coined discrete-time quantum walk with coin applied before the shift
Reflecting (coin-flip) rule at broken edges and chain boundaries
Hadamard coin for the one-dimensional chain
Instance parameters N=4, p=1/2, initial state |1,R> are chosen by the reconstruction, not taken from the abstract
Attractor theory for random unitary maps is recalled as background and is not verified here
